item.title: A 'wow' player - why Ngumoha is already a Liverpool game-changer
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

A 'wow' player - why Ngumoha is already a Liverpool game-changer

Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he showed everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just shows how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

Yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still showed all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

'An important day for a positive mindset'

There were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so important for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a big week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

- Published5 hours ago

Source: BBC Sport | Published: 2026-11-22 23:20 UTC

item.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.

Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and Peter Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.

Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.

Atlético Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe.

Diego Simeone’s side are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off Real Madrid. Álex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julián Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Álex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sørloth.

In Serie A, Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the title pace despite Pio Esposito’s hat-trick.

Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic’s penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito’s goals, but Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessié penalty salvaged a point.

It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season, but kept Cristian Chivu’s side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.

Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter’s lead by heading home from a corner. Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.

De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta’s fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic’s spot-kick.

That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessié calmly converted.

Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.

Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”

Milan returned to the top four as Gonçalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone.

Ruben Amorim’s side sealed back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month to go fourth, five points behind leaders Lazio, as club record signing Ramos broke a five-match goalless streak.

Milan got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes. Amorim accused his players of “not helping Ramos” before the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

His third was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaká in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.

The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counterattacking as substitutes Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse struck before Christian Pulisic’s dinked finish completed the biggest victory of the Amorim era.

Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals Paris Saint-Germain with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.…

Source: The Guardian Sport | Published: 2026-11-22 22:20 UTC

PGA Tour: Rasmus Hojgaard shares lead at weather-affected RSM Classic as FedExCup Fall finale heads to Monday finish

Sunday 22 November 2026 22:43, UK

Rasmus Hojgaard holds a share of the lead heading into a weather-delayed final day of the RSM Classic, with England's Marco Penge in contention as he looks to secure his PGA Tour future.

Hojgaard entered the week 122nd in the FedExCup standings and among the players looking to break into the top 100 and remain fully exempt on the PGA Tour next season, with the Dane now in prime position to do that.

The Ryder Cup star posted a five-under 65 on the Seaside Course at Sea Island Golf Club, firing five birdies to move to 13 under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen, with Max Greyserman a shot off the pace in third.

The Dane carded back-to-back birdies from the sixth and followed a 10-foot birdie at the 12th by holing from 30 feet for another at the 16th, before closing a blemish-free day by draining a 25-footer at the par-four last to move joint-top of the leaderboard.

"Today felt very free - tomorrow's a completely different day," Hojgaard said. "I'm going to feel the nerves. I think that's what we all play for is to put ourselves in those positions, and we'll see what happens."

Penge needs at least a top-four finish to have a chance of breaking inside the top 100, with a two-under 68 keeping him within two of the lead heading into a second successive Monday finish on the PGA Tour.

Haotong Li and Max McGreevy join Penge on 11 under, while Jackson Koivun is in the group three strokes back with Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen and Belgium's Adrien Dumont de Chassart.

The tournament was washed out by heavy rain on Saturday, leading to the final round being held on Monday. The Austin Championship last week also was delayed by rain, marking the first time since 2015 that successive PGA Tour events have been dragged into an unscheduled fifth day.

Those 51st to 60th in the FedExCup standings after this week qualify for the first two Signature Events of 2027, while those who end between 101st and 125th on the PGA Tour only receive conditional status and will be unable to feature in certain events.

The final round starts on Monday at 7.20am local time (12.20pm UK time), with a two-tee start in operation and players going out in threeballs.

item.title: Gerwyn Price ends four-year barren run with Grand Slam of Darts win in Wolverhampton
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Gerwyn Price finally ended his major trophy drought by winning the Grand Slam of Darts and is delighted to silence his critics. The Welshman had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.

But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton. Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the fourth time, but this one will surely mean the most to him.

The 41-year-old, who swatted away a wasp and Kevin Doets in the semi-finals earlier on Sunday, was embroiled in a tense and nervy encounter which turned in the 15th leg. Van Veen had six darts to break for an 8-7 lead, but could not finish and Price seized the moment. He took out double two on his fifth attempt to win the leg and then reeled off the next six to take control.

It was an imperious period of play which left Van Veen with no way back as “the Iceman” coolly saw out the win to get back into the winners’ circle – his eighth major title.

His lack of silverware has been a talking point and he is happy to end the noise. “I was probably more nervous in this game than ever,” he said. “I’ve lost so many finals. Just to keep the media off my back, it’s not for me.

“I do mind and I don’t mind, but now they can stop talking about it. I’m going to Minehead next week with a major, so they can leave me alone. I’ve had some close calls this year where I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it comes along, it’s nice.”

Van Veen has also not won a major in a while, but his chances were limited against a player who he has a poor record against. “I don’t like Gezzy,” Van Veen, who earlier ended compatriot Michael van Gerwen’s hopes of winning, joked. “Gezzy, I don’t like you.

“I think it was a very close game. He took out a lot of good finishes with me waiting, and I missed a couple of chances.

“So I think the 16-11 was a flattered scoreline. It’s part of the job and that’s what Gezzy does. He always puts everyone under pressure, and he took his chances, and that’s why he deserves to win. I’m very devastated.”

Source: The Guardian Sport | Published: 2026-11-22 21:54 UTC

Thitikul wins third title in a row at LPGA finale

CME Group Tour Championship - final leaderboard

-24 J Thitikul (Tha); -22 A Iwai (Jap); -20 N Korda (US); -19 P Anannarukarn (Tha), Y Liu (Chn)

Selected others: -16 M Stark (Swe); -14 L Woad (Eng); -13 C Hull (Eng); -4 L Maguire (Ire)

World number two Jeeno Thitikul produced a seven-under final round of 65 to claim a third successive CME Group Tour Championship title.

The 23-year-old from Thailand started the fourth round of the season-ending event with an eagle and went on to card five birdies as she finished on 24 under at the Tiburon Golf Club in Florida.

"The only words I have is not to change the course until I'm retired," said Thitikul.

"It's just me and the course, we just are best friends. I think she is my best friend on the tour."

Her victory earned the $4m (Â£3.1m) top prize and also broke Annika Sorenstam's career earnings record of $22,583,693 to become the tour's all-time prize money leader on $24,292,858.

Japan's Akie Iwai also carded a 65 in the fourth round to claim second place on 22 under, while American Nelly Korda's 68 put her third on 20 under.

World number one Korda also overtook Sorenstam to move to second on the LPGA Tour career prize money list.

South Korea's A-Lim Kim had an overnight lead of one shot but her challenge faltered after a double bogey and bogey on the first three holes as she finished with a 72 and tied seventh.

England's Lottie Woad carded a 67 to end on 14 under, with compatriot Charley Hull one shot further back after a 73 in the final round.

item.title: Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup

Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup.

A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.

The tournament would involve 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

Nineteen venues are proposed by the 'All Together' bid, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Fifa's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five. However, its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed that "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

This is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

Fifa's bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

England hosted the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland are also joint hosts of the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it will still be considered in its current form.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it."

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

The Irish Football Association's chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country. Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that."

Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow are the Scottish venues proposed, with Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell saying hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."

The special meeting of Fifa's Congress is also set to approve the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Source: BBC Sport | Published: 2026-11-22 21:44 UTC
